title: Window Functions
interviewAnswer: Window functions compute values across related rows without collapsing them. Common examples are ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG, LEAD and running aggregates using OVER(PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...).
why: Window functions are a common SQL interview discriminator because they solve ranking, lag/lead and rolling calculations without collapsing row-level detail.
intuition: GROUP BY reduces many rows into one row per group. A window function keeps the original rows but lets each row look across a defined set of neighboring rows.
deepDive: The OVER clause defines the window. PARTITION BY resets calculations by group; ORDER BY defines sequence; a frame such as ROWS BETWEEN controls which ordered rows contribute. ROW_NUMBER assigns unique positions, RANK leaves gaps after ties, DENSE_RANK does not. LAG/LEAD access prior/future rows and are useful for temporal features.
workedExample: To find each customer’s latest order, assign ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date DESC) and keep row_number=1. This avoids a separate aggregate-plus-join pattern.
commonMistakes: Confusing PARTITION BY with GROUP BY.
Ignoring tie behavior between ROW_NUMBER, RANK and DENSE_RANK.
Using LAG/LEAD without an explicit, meaningful ordering.
followUps: How do you calculate a running average?
production: Window functions are useful in feature generation, deduplication and event sequencing, but large partitions/orderings can be expensive; inspect execution plans and partition strategies.
